text:
Predicates:
Conductor(x) ::: x is a conductor.
Leads(x, y) ::: x leads y.
Orchestra(y) ::: y is an orchestra.
Wrote(x, y) ::: x wrote y.
Premiered(y, z) ::: y premiered in z.
MusicPiece(y) ::: y is a music piece.
Compose(x, y) ::: x writes y.
Instrument(y) ::: y is a music instrument.
Perform(y, z) ::: y premiered by z.
ViennaMusicSociety(z) ::: z is the Vienna Music Society.
PremiereYear(y, z) ::: y was premiered in year z.
Specialize(x, y) ::: x specializes in y.
Musical(x) ::: x is music.
Music(y) ::: y is music.
Beethoven(x) ::: x is Beethoven.
Symphony9(y) ::: y is Symphony No. 9.
Premiere(z, y) ::: z premiered y.
Lead(x, y) ::: x leads y.
---------------------
Premises:
MusicPiece(Symphony9) ::: Symphony No. 9 is a music piece.
Compose(x, y) ∧ MusicPiece(y) ::: Composers write music pieces.
Wrote(Beethoven, Symphony9) ::: Beethoven wrote Symphony No. 9.
Premiered(Symphony9, ViennaMusicSociety) ::: Vienna Music Society premiered Symphony No. 9.
ViennaMusicSociety(ViennaMusicSociety) ::: Vienna Music Society is an orchestra.
Leads(Beethoven, ViennaMusicSociety) ::: Beethoven leads the Vienna Music Society.
Orchestra(y) → ∃x (Conductor(x) ∧ Leads(x, y)) ::: Orchestras are led by conductors.
---------------------
Conclusion:
¬Conductor(Beethoven) ::: Beethoven is not a conductor.
